Preliminary Remarks
You have decided to study at the University of Bern or you are
considering registering. This brochure informs you in detail if your
upper secondary school-leaving certificate and/or higher education
qualifications allow you to study at the University of Bern.
The University Law (UniG) of 5 September 1996, the University
Ordinance (UniV) of 12 September 2012 and the University Statute
(UniSt) of 7 June 2011 as well as the regulations pertaining to them
are the legal foundation documents of this brochure. According to
article 11 para. 2 of the University Ordinance, the admission
requirements for prospective students with foreign qualifications
were adopted and confirmed respectively at the session of the
University Directorate on 9 December 2025.
All foundation documents are available online in the legal docu-
ments collection of the Legal Services Department
www.rechtsdienst.unibe.ch.

1 Introduction
6 Admission requirements University of Bern
1.1 Validity of these admission requirements
These admission requirements are valid for the academic year 2026/2027
only.
1.2 Principles
Swiss and foreign qualifications can be fully or partly recognised for either
all, for all non-medical, or for certain courses of study. The recognised
foreign upper secondary school-leaving certificates and higher education
qualifications are listed in chapters 4 and 5.
1.3 Compulsory registration
(UniV, www.belex.sites.be.ch/data/436.111.1/de, art. 6 and follow-
ing articles)
All students have to be registered. Those who are not registered may not
make use of university services, i.e. they may neither attend lectures nor
undergo assessments. There are special regulations for students who are
registered at another institution of higher education and who are - on the
basis of an agreement - completing a part of their studies at the University
of Bern (see BeNeFri, mobility programmes, swissuniversities agreements
and so on).
Doctoral students have to be matriculated over the entire period they are
supervised.
1.4 Non-admission
(UniV, www.belex.sites.be.ch/data/436.111.1/de, art. 14)
Prospective students who are definitely not allowed to continue their
studies in a degree course at another Swiss or foreign university or institu-
tion of higher education because of failure in assessments may not be
admitted to studies in this degree course at the University of Bern. Simulta-
neous registration at another Swiss university at the same level of study is
generally not permitted. Applications for admission will be rejected in
cases of dishonesty or if prohibitions or regulations in the legal ordinance
are violated. This includes especially false or incomplete information and/or
submission of forged diplomas, certificates, study evidences and other
documents.
1.5 Visiting students and visiting doctoral students
(UniV, www.belex.sites.be.ch/data/436.111.1/de, art. 7)
Students or doctoral students who are registered or on leave of absence at
a recognised foreign university can register and undergo assessments at
the University of Bern for two semesters at the most. Courses and assess-
ments of degree programmes which are subject to restrictions on admis-
sions are excepted. These student’s university entrance qualifications or
Academic year 2026/2027 7
academic achievements are not scrutinised.
1.6 Auditors
(UniV, www.belex.sites.be.ch/data/436.111.1/de, art. 8)
Adults of 18 years of age and above may register as auditors to attend
lectures and seminars. They have no right to academic assessments and
cannot earn ECTS credits. Courses attended as an auditor cannot be
counted toward a degree. The registration takes place each semester and is
chargeable. Auditors of lectures have to register by 30 September for the
fall semester respectively 28 February for the spring semester.
1.7 Aptitude tests
swissuniversities sets an aptitude test for entry to the study of medicine,
dental medicine and veterinary medicine in early July whenever the
number of applications exceeds the number of places.
It is expected that an aptitude test will be conducted for entry to the
Bachelor of Sports Science Major and Minor (60 ECTS credits) in spring, if
the number of applications exceeds the number of places.
1.8 Language Test and Language Certificate
Candidates who wish to enroll in a bachelor’s program at the University of
Bern and are not native speakers of German must provide proof of suffi-
cient knowledge of the German language (level C1).
The University of Bern offers a German language test approximately three
weeks before the beginning of the lecture period of the fall semester.
Provided that the application for studies was made in due time and
candidates have received a corresponding admission decree, registration
for the German test is done via the Admissions Office by July 31 at the
latest. Enrollment will only take place after the German language test has
been passed. Applicants with a Swiss university entrance qualification or
study permit are generally exempt from proving sufficient language skills
(cf. German test regulations).
Certain Master’s programs require proof of excellent German or English
skills (cf. study regulations and plans of studies of the various study pro-
grams).

4 Admission at doctoral level
12 Admission requirements University of Bern
(UniV, www.belex.sites.be.ch/data/436.111.1/de, art. 31)
In order to be admitted to a doctoral programme, applicants must have a
master’s degree from a recognized university on the basis of a bachelor’s
degree of a minimum of three years or an equivalent degree from a state
or officially recognized university (compare also chapter 5.1 below, which
applies to admission on MA level).
The University of Bern regulates the permeability between the various
types of Swiss Higher Education Institutions in the Regulations governing
the admission to the university with a degree from a university of applied
sciences or a university of teacher education by the Rector’s Office of 26
April 2022 or in the overview attached (published on the Internet).
Admission without a listed degree is not possible.
Any other requirements set out by the relevant faculty or graduate school
(e.g. specific average grade or a specific result in the degree) must also be
fulfilled.
Admission to doctoral studies with continuing education qualifications
(Master of Advanced Studies, Executive Master or similar) is not possible.

5 Foreign entrance qualifications
14 Admission requirements University of Bern
(Decision of the Executive Board of 9 December 2025 based upon art. 11
of the UniV, www.belex.sites.be.ch/data/436.111.1/de)
5.1 Principles
Applicants holding foreign university degrees can be admitted without
restriction to all degree courses as long as they hold a recognised univer-
sity degree at bachelor’s level (full-time study programme over a period of
at least three years) or a master’s degree based on a bachelor’s degree of
at least three years full-time or a degree at licentiate level (minimum
duration of study: 4.5 years full-time). A university degree is only consid-
ered acceptable if it was acquired as part of a successfully completed
academic degree course at a state or state-recognised university.
Degrees from distance-learning universities1 are recognised only if the
applicant can produce evidence of a study place on the corresponding
master’s degree course at a regular state or state-recognised university
entitled to award doctorates in the same country and if the degree course
does not vary in content from a regular degree course at a state or
state-recognised university.
Degrees which were acquired at a foreign campus of a state or state-rec-
ognised university will be recognised only if the foreign campus is also
recognised by the State. Degrees which are issued for coursework at
several universities (especially diplomas acquired by Transnational Educa-
tion diplomas) will be accepted only if all coursework has been completed
at recognised universities, and at least half of the credits must have been
acquired at the university which issues the degree2.
Continuing education qualifications (Master of Advanced Studies, Execu-
tive Master) and degrees from universities of applied sciences3 (engineer-
ing schools, technical schools, schools for paramedical professions, music,
art or foreign language schools, interpreter training schools, agricultural
schools, hospitality and tourism management schools, etc.) and degrees
from institutions which have agreements with a recognised university in
another country will not be accepted for admission.
5.2 Admission to master’s degree programmes
Prospective students who have acquired a recognised bachelor’s degree
(minimum duration of study: 3 years full-time) at a recognised foreign
university according to chapter 5.1 are eligible for admission to a succes-
1 The same additional requirements apply for distance learning universities of applied
sciences from signatory states of the Lisbon convention.
2 Exceptions are degrees obtained as part of ENLIGHT.
3 Exception: degrees from officially recognized universities of applied sciences of signatory
states of the Lisbon convention, provided they do not significantly differ from their Swiss
equivalents, i.e. degrees from Swiss universities of applied science.
Academic year 2026/2027 15
sive non-medical master’s programme in the relevant field of study at the
University of Bern provided that the master’s degree can be successfully
completed with an additional maximum of 60 ECTS credits and indepen-
dent of their upper secondary school-leaving certificate. The course
regulations of the relevant master degree programmes define the maxi-
mum age of a diploma. Additional entry requirements may be specified in
the study plans of individual master’s degree courses, and the completion
of a master’s degree course can be made dependent on the evidence of
further skills and abilities.
Specialised master’s degree programmes may be subject to additional
admission requirements.
Applications for the recognition of study periods and achievements have
to be addressed to the Admissions Office. International agreements
(Bologna Declaration, Lisbon Agreement and bilateral agreements with
Germany, France, Austria, Italy and so on) must be considered.
Prospective students must see that the prerequisites required in individual
cases are fulfilled. On request, a proof has to be provided that they were
not excluded or dismissed from university because of failure in assess-
ments or other reasons.
At the University of Bern, some master’s degree programmes are offered
in English language. Other courses of study are mainly held in German.
Regarding the language test and language certificate, see chapter 1.8. If
no language certificate is required for the desired Master’s program, it is
the applicants’ responsibility to ensure that they are proficient in the
language of instruction.
Applicants who must complete elements in a preceding bachelor’s degree
course to attain a degree at master’s level in the same field of study will
usually need a very good knowledge of German.
5.3 Admission to bachelor’s degree programmes
The list of countries under chapter 5.8 provides information about the
admission qualifications which give access to all non-medical courses of
study at the University of Bern. The faculties decide on the transfer of
credits (as part of the assessment).
In cases of certificates which have not been recognised, prospective
students may need to pass an exam for a full Swiss or a cantonal upper
secondary school-leaving certificate recognised by the Confederation.
Regarding the language test and language certificate, see
chapter 1.8.
16 Admission requirements University of Bern
5.4 General requirements for upper secondary school-leaving
certificates
5.4.1 Qualifications or upper secondary school-leaving certificates from
other countries have to meet the following requirements. They must
1. be of general educational character,
2. have been acquired after completion of at least 12 school years, of
which at least 3 years at academic upper secondary school,
3. show an emphasis on Classical Languages, Modern Languages,
Humanities and Social Sciences or Mathematics/Natural Sciences,
4. represent the highest possible level of upper secondary school in
the country awarding the diploma,
5. grant admission to all university faculties and to all branches of
study in the country awarding the diploma and
6. have been acquired in a full-time, class-based course of instruc-
tion. In justified cases, the Executive Board of the university may
waive this criterion.

5.4.4 Applicants have to fulfil the conditions required in each individual
case according to the following list of countries. Upon request, proof
must be supplied that no exclusion or expulsion from another
university has occurred as a result of failed performance assessments
or for other reasons.
5.5 Supplementary examination (entry at bachelor’s level)
The upper secondary school-leaving certificates of some countries are
accepted only together with a supplementary examination. The supple-
mentary examination is held once a year before the start of the fall
semester; see www.bachelor.unibe.ch/eng → Application and Admission.
Application deadline and examination dates
www.bachelor.unibe.ch/supplementaryexamination:
Application dead- written oral

15 June calendar week 33 calendar week 35
Applicants can only take the supplementary examination with a confirma-
tion from the University of Bern that their qualifications in combination
with a pass at the supplementary examination are sufficient for the
desired degree. For this reason, a complete application must be sent to
the Admissions Office.
Academic year 2026/2027 19
The examination consists of five subjects:
• The language of instruction: German. As an exception, French may be
chosen as language of instruction. Even in this case, a proof of adequate
knowledge of the German language has to be provided. The knowledge
of the German language is decisive.
• 3 compulsory subjects: Mathematics, English and History (including
introduction to Law)
• 1 compulsory subject from the following group: Biology, Chemistry,
Physics or Geography (including introduction to Economics)
5.6 Proof of admission
Proof of admission must be issued for the desired field of study by a state
or state-recognized university with the right to award doctorates in the
country of origin of the school leaving certificate (not a distance learning
university) and must not be older than one year. In justified cases, the
university management may waive a proof of study place.
5.7 Upper secondary school-leaving certificates of the
individual countries
The upper secondary school-leaving certificates of the individual countries
are assessed on the basis of the following pre-requisites:
5.7.1 Recommendations for the assessment of foreign upper secondary
school-leaving certificates
These guidelines were adopted on November 11 2021 by the
Chamber of universities of swissuniversities. They are reviewed
regularly.
5.7.2 Lisbon Convention
The parties to the Lisbon Convention mutually recognise those
qualifications which enable their holders to access higher educa-
tion in the country of issue.
Compensations are defined in case of a substantial difference in
the assessment of foreign upper secondary school-leaving certifi-
cates.
According to articles IV.4 and IV.5, the admission to a certain higher
education programme can be made dependent on the fulfilment of
additional specific requirements (e.g. special faculty admission or
proof of admission to higher education).
5.7.3 University Convention No. 15/1953
20 Admission requirements University of Bern
5.7.4 Bilateral agreements
Bilateral agreements about university equivalencies exist with
Germany, Austria, France and Italy. On the basis of these agree-
ments, prospective students can be admitted to a degree course in
their former field, independently of their previous qualifications, if
they have already successfully completed an important part of their
degree course (usually to the extent of stage I studies or a bachelor
degree) with an intermediate test (not a single-subject examina-
tion) at a recognised German, Austrian, French or Italian university.
However, aptitude and language tests may have to be taken. The
Bernese faculty in question recognises completed study areas in
their decision on placement in accordance with the agreements.
5.8 Admission requirements by country - academic year
2026/2027
Regarding the definition of school-leaving certificate, supplementary
examination and language certificate, see previous chapters.
5.8.1 International upper secondary school-leaving certificates
1. The Baccalauréat Européen is recognised, if the school-leaving
certificate complies with the list of subjects according to chapter
5.4.2.
2. The Baccalauréat International is recognised, if the school-leav-
ing certificate shows 32 out of 42 points (without bonus points)
and 6 subjects according to chapter 5.4.2. At least 3 subjects must
be in the Higher Level, of which at least 1 in Mathematics or
another scientific subject (subject group 3 or 4).
